newsitem.title: USA: Fortune to accept classified ads for first time.
newsitem.headline: Fortune to accept classified ads for first time.

text.p: Fortune, the bi-weekly business magazine, said Tuesday that it will for the first time accept classified ads.
Among the other changes, Fortune said it will beef up its "Personal Fortune" section and will add two new sections -- information technology, called "Digital Watch" and a "Smart Managing" section.
The magazine, which officially hits the newstands next Monday, will also be one-inch narrower while its length will stay the same.
It said that the changes have been made based on readers' response and research over the past year.
"For 18 months we have worked to increase the utility, the relevance and the entertainment value of everything we do," said Managing Editor John Huey.

"We have broadened the scope of subjects we cover while honing our expertise in narrower areas of interest, such as information technology, and we have added a variety of voices to the magazine," he said.
A 15-word classifed ad will cost $210 and display classified, $650 per inch.
